bpx.hero.h1: First steps after a diabetes diagnosis
bpx.hero.lede: Starting from the title of the clinic's Facebook post — what to do first when you learn you have diabetes, in calm, general language.
bpx.intro.p1: On 11 April 2019, the clinic's Facebook page published this post, and it began with a question. The post carried only that title; so, as a patient-friendly answer to the question, a few calm, general points are laid out here — with no numeric targets and no treatment instructions.
bpx.intro.attr: “You have learned you have diabetes — what will you do.” — the clinic's Facebook post, 11 April 2019
bpx.first.p1: When you learn that you have diabetes, the first task is one — see a doctor as soon as possible. The doctor will run tests to understand your condition and advise what you should do. Listen carefully to the advice, and follow it.
bpx.first.p2: Do not start buying and taking medicines from a pharmacy on your own — that path can be risky. What medicine diabetes needs and when to start it — these decisions belong to the doctor alone. There is nothing embarrassing about it; getting advice on time is a good start.
bpx.food.p: Some general habits around food and daily routine are considered helpful for many people — but which one suits your body, and by how much, only your doctor can say, knowing your condition:
bpx.food.1: Regular, moderate and balanced meals — eating on a schedule rather than a lot at once
bpx.food.2: Cutting down sugary drinks — soft drinks, bottled juice, sugar in tea or coffee
bpx.food.3: Some walking every day — considered generally helpful; talk to your doctor before starting
bpx.food.4: Trying to avoid smoking or tobacco use — tell your doctor if you need help
bpx.med.p: If the doctor has prescribed medicines, the way is to take them properly and on schedule. Do not reduce, increase, stop or change any medicine on your own — even when you feel well. Any question or difficulty about medicines, tell the doctor; the decision is theirs too.
bpx.foot.p1: Long-standing diabetes can affect different organs of the body — the feet and the eyes are especially notable among them. So keeping up regular tests matters; the doctor will also decide which test is needed and how often.
bpx.foot.p2: This point matters especially for this clinic's patients too — in any anorectal treatment, what counts most is the wound healing properly, and when diabetes is present, careful watch becomes even more important. So if you have diabetes, tell the treating doctor before treatment begins.
bpx.urgent.p: Any unusual or rapidly worsening symptom — severe weakness, feeling faint, or a wound that is not healing — take a doctor's advice without delay. If the situation seems serious, go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Rather than any list, the advice of a doctor who knows your condition is the reliable one.
